patients.summary: Office manager with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and lithium-treated bipolar I disorder who joined in 2022. His first colonoscopy found a stage IIA ascending colon cancer, resected without chemotherapy; lithium then caused nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and an NSTEMI with an LAD stent followed, then stable angina, epistaxis, a left retinal detachment and in 2026 a right lateral medullary stroke.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Friedman phoned about membership. Lives in town, his previous internist retired in the spring and he has been without a PCP since. Membership packet emailed. New patient visit set for 8/16 at 8:40. He signed the release over the phone portal; records request sent to the prior office for the last 3 years of notes, labs and immunizations. He asked whether we coordinate with his psychiatrist, told yes once he signs a release for that office too.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records from prior internal medicine office received, 41 pages, abstracted for PCP.

Problems on their list: essential hypertension (on lisinopril since about 2012), hyperlipidemia, bipolar I disorder followed by outside psychiatry, knee osteoarthritis.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily (psychiatry prescribes).
Allergies: none known.
Immunizations: Tdap 2017; influenza most years.
Labs 2021: BMP normal, lithium 0.7, TSH normal, lipids on atorvastatin with LDL in the high 90s.
No colonoscopy or stool test on record.

Scanned to media tab.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

58M, office manager, transferring care after his prior internist retired. Feels well. Here mostly to get established and get his refills under one roof.

HTN: on lisinopril 20 for about ten years, home cuff readings in the low 130s. No headaches, no chest symptoms.
Lipids: atorvastatin 40 qhs, no muscle aches.
Bipolar I: lithium 300 bid, prescribed by his psychiatrist, whom he sees about once a year. Last mood episode was well before he started lithium. Sleeping fine, working full time.
Knees: achy with stairs and after long walks, both sides on and off. Walks most mornings, gave up running years ago. Uses nothing for it.

PMH/meds as above. PSH: none. NKDA.
Family: father had an MI at 55 and high blood pressure; mother has type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol; a paternal uncle had a stroke at 60; maternal grandfather had colon polyps.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks a week, no drugs. Office manager. Eats reasonably well.
Prevention: has never had a colonoscopy or stool test. Tdap 2017.

ROS otherwise negative.

EXAM: well-appearing, BMI about 27. HEENT unremarkable, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Knees with mild crepitus, no effusion, full range. No tremor. Neuro grossly normal. Mood euthymic, affect full.

A/P
1. Essential hypertension, controlled. Continue lisinopril 20.
2. Hyperlipidemia. Continue atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
3. Bipolar I on lithium, stable. Lithium level, BMP, TSH, calcium today. Will copy psychiatry on results once release is signed.
4. Knee OA, mild. Activity as tolerated.
5. Health maintenance: overdue for colon cancer screening; he prefers colonoscopy, referral to GI placed. Hep C and HIV screening today. Shingrix and flu/COVID this fall at a nurse visit. PHQ-9 2.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Patrick, your labs from Tuesday look good. Kidney function, sodium and calcium are normal, thyroid is normal, and your lithium level is 0.7, squarely in the usual range. Cholesterol is about where it has been on atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. GI should call you to set up the colonoscopy; let us know if you don't hear from them in two weeks.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seen before work for flu, bivalent COVID booster and first Shingrix. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, Shingrix L deltoid lower site. Tolerated, waited 15 min. Told him Shingrix can make the arm sore and him tired for a day or two. Dose 2 due in 2 to 6 months, scheduled for December. Colonoscopy is booked for January per patient.

documents.title: Psychiatry annual letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry. Date of service 11/02/2022.

Dear colleague, thank you for the release. I have followed Mr. Friedman for bipolar I disorder since 2013, when lithium was started; he has had no mood episodes on it and works full time. Today he is euthymic, sleeping well, no side effects beyond occasional dry mouth. No tremor.

Plan: continue lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily. I would appreciate a lithium level with BMP, TSH and calcium every 3 to 4 months; please send them my way. Avoid NSAIDs and let me know of any change in his blood pressure medicines, since ACE inhibitors and diuretics can raise lithium levels. I will see him yearly.

Outpatient psychiatrist

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Shingrix #2, lab draw
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix given R deltoid. After the first dose he had a sore arm and felt run-down for an evening, nothing more. Lithium level and BMP drawn, 12-hour trough (last dose 8 pm). Series complete.

documents.title: Lithium and BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lithium 0.8, BMP unremarkable. Copy to psychiatry. Next level in March.

reports.text:
A. Ascending colon mass, biopsies: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.
B. Sigmoid colon polyp, snare: tubular adenoma, no high-grade dysplasia.
C. Descending colon polyp, snare: tubular adenoma, no high-grade dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. Two tubular adenomas.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report and pathology
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology. Procedure date 01/10/2023.
Indication: first colonoscopy, age 58, referred for screening.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good.

Findings: An ulcerated, partly circumferential mass about 3.5 cm in the ascending colon, roughly 6 cm distal to the ileocecal valve, biopsied and tattooed distally. A 7 mm sessile polyp in the sigmoid and a 5 mm sessile polyp in the descending colon, both removed by cold snare. Terminal ileum normal. Small internal hemorrhoids.

Impression: ascending colon mass suspicious for malignancy; two small polyps removed.
Plan: await pathology; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and CEA for staging; colorectal surgery referral.

Pathology (01/12/2023): ascending colon biopsies show invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Both polyps tubular adenomas.

Received by fax; PCP notified.

documents.title: Colonoscopy pathology discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Patrick after reviewing the GI report. He had already heard from the gastroenterologist yesterday that the biopsy showed cancer. Spent about 20 minutes. Went over what happens next: staging CT scans and a blood marker next week, then a surgeon. Explained that many colon cancers found this way are cured with surgery alone, but we won't know his stage until the scans and the operation. He is shaken but practical, wants to keep working. Offered to see him any time; he will message after the CT. Lithium: told him to keep taking it and that we'll coordinate with psychiatry around surgery.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Lungs clear without nodules or masses. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Heart normal in size; no pericardial or pleural effusion. Osseous structures unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Focal circumferential wall thickening of the ascending colon measuring about 3.6 cm in length, corresponding to the known mass, with mild adjacent fat stranding. No enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymph nodes. Liver without focal lesion. Spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites. Bladder and prostate unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon mass without nodal or distant metastasis.

documents.title: Staging CT and CEA
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Outside imaging and lab, 01/18/2023. CT chest and CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast for staging of ascending colon adenocarcinoma: known ascending colon mass, no adenopathy, no liver or lung lesions. CEA 2.6 ng/mL (reference under 3.0). Reports filed under imaging. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Colorectal surgery consultation
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Colorectal surgery clinic. Seen 01/26/2023.

Reason: ascending colon adenocarcinoma found at first colonoscopy.

58-year-old office manager, asymptomatic, no bleeding, no change in stool, no weight loss. HTN, hyperlipidemia, bipolar disorder on lithium. No prior abdominal surgery. Never smoker. Allergies: NKDA. Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily.

Exam: BMI 27, abdomen soft and nontender without masses.
Staging: CT without metastatic disease; CEA 2.6.

Impression: clinical stage I-II adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon.
Plan: laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis, booked 02/21. Enhanced recovery pathway. Hold lisinopril the morning of surgery. Lithium to be held the day of surgery and resumed when drinking; level on postoperative day 1. We have notified his psychiatrist.

events.reason: Right hemicolectomy for ascending colon adenocarcinoma

reports.text: Right colon, laparoscopic right hemicolectomy: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, 3.8 cm, arising in the ascending colon. Tumor invades through the muscularis propria into pericolonic fat (pT3). No lymphovascular or perineural invasion. Margins negative. Nineteen lymph nodes negative (0/19). No tumor deposits. Mismatch repair proteins MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6 retained (proficient). Prior biopsy site and tattoo identified. Terminal ileum and appendix unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Colon adenocarcinoma, pT3 pN0 (0/19), margins negative, MMR proficient: AJCC stage IIA.

documents.title: Discharge summary - right hemicolectomy
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 02/21/2023, discharged 02/24/2023.

Procedure 02/21: laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with stapled primary ileocolic anastomosis for ascending colon adenocarcinoma. Uncomplicated.

Course: enhanced recovery pathway. Clear liquids the evening of surgery, regular diet on day 2, flatus day 2, bowel movement day 3. Pain controlled with acetaminophen and a brief course of oral oxycodone, which he stopped before discharge. Lithium held the morning of surgery and resumed that evening; level 0.7 on day 1. Lisinopril resumed day 1. Ambulating independently.

Pathology: pT3 N0 (0/19 nodes), margins negative, MMR proficient, stage IIA.

Discharge meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic in 2 weeks; medical oncology referral placed to discuss adjuvant therapy; PCP within 1 to 2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - after hemicolectomy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Nine days out from laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (2/21) for ascending colon adenocarcinoma. Final path pT3 N0, 0/19 nodes, MMR proficient, stage IIA. Eating normally, stools soft and a bit more frequent than before, no blood. Incisions sore with getting up, taking acetaminophen once a day. Off the oxycodone. Walking around the block. Has oncology on 3/29 to talk about whether chemo adds anything. Mood steady.

O: Afebrile, vitals as charted. Port sites and periumbilical extraction incision clean, dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the incision, bowel sounds present. Calves soft.

A/P: Recovering well after right hemicolectomy, stage IIA colon cancer. Activity: no lifting over 10 lb until surgeon clears. Back to desk work part-time next week if he feels up to it. Continue lisinopril, atorvastatin, lithium unchanged; hospital lithium level was 0.7. We'll see what oncology recommends.

documents.title: Medical oncology follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical oncology clinic, visit 03/29/2023.

Mr. Friedman returns, five weeks after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy, to decide about adjuvant chemotherapy for stage IIA (pT3 N0, 0/19 nodes) adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, MMR proficient, no lymphovascular invasion, negative margins, no obstruction or perforation. He is concerned about how much chemotherapy would actually help him versus what it would cost him in side effects.

History: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, bipolar I disorder on lithium. Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily. NKDA. Never smoker, social alcohol, office manager. Father MI at 55; mother type 2 diabetes; maternal grandfather colon polyps.

BP 132/84. Exam unremarkable; incisions healed.
Labs today: hemoglobin 13.2, WBC 7.2, platelets 250, creatinine 1.0, AST 28, ALT 30.

Assessment and plan: Stage IIA colon cancer without high-risk features. We reviewed that adjuvant fluoropyrimidine reduces recurrence risk only modestly in this setting, and that MMR-proficient, low-risk stage II disease is commonly observed. After discussion he prefers surveillance without chemotherapy, which I support.
Surveillance: visit with CEA every 6 months for 2 years then less often; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis yearly for 3 years (first in February 2024); colonoscopy one year after surgery.

Medical oncology

documents.title: Oncology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to let you know the oncologist and I agreed on no chemo, just scans and blood tests. Honestly relieved. Back at work full days. Do I need to do anything different on my end?

documents.title: RE: Oncology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's good news and I agree with the plan; I have her letter. Nothing different on your end. Keep the oncology schedule, and we'll keep doing your lithium labs here. Your next one is due now, so stop by the lab any morning this month.

documents.title: Lithium monitoring
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lithium 0.8, BMP and TSH normal. Faxed to psychiatry.

orders.order: BMP, serum and urine osmolality, urinalysis, lithium level

documents.title: Up all night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Not urgent but it's getting old. For about 2 months I've been up 5 or 6 times a night to pee and I'm thirsty all the time, I keep a big water bottle at my desk and still feel dry. No burning. Could this be the surgery? Or sugar, my mom has diabetes.

documents.title: RE: Up all night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. It's worth checking soon. I put in blood and urine tests, please go Monday morning (you can eat and drink normally), and I'll see you Wednesday 6/21 at 9:20 to go over them. If you get confused, very weak, or can't keep fluids down, go to the ED.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - polyuria, thirst
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: urinating constantly, always thirsty.

HPI: Two months of large-volume urination day and night, now up 5-6 times nightly, and a thirst he can't satisfy; goes through several liters of water a day and prefers it ice cold. No dysuria, hematuria, weak stream or dribbling. No weight loss. Bowels have settled since the hemicolectomy in February. Has been on lithium about ten years for bipolar I, mood stable throughout, no dose changes, no NSAIDs, no new meds. Also says he snores loudly enough that he's been sent to the couch, and he nods off in afternoon meetings; he blames the broken sleep but admits the snoring predates this.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, lithium 300 bid. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Mucous membranes dry. Neck thick, Mallampati 3. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen healed incisions, no bladder distension. No edema. No tremor.

Labs Monday: Na 146 (high), serum osm 300, urine osm 150, urine SG 1.005, glucose and calcium normal, lithium 0.8. Urine glucose negative.

A/P
1. Polyuria with dilute urine despite high serum sodium and osmolality, normal glucose and calcium, on long-term lithium: lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Explained the mechanism. Drink to thirst, do not restrict water. Nephrology referral for confirmation (desmopressin challenge) and treatment options. Will talk with his psychiatrist about lithium; he is very reluctant to change something that has worked for a decade.
2. Snoring, daytime sleepiness, HTN: likely OSA. Home sleep apnea test ordered.
3. HTN, lipids: no change.

Call me after nephrology.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology. Seen 07/19/2023 at PCP request.

59M with bipolar I disorder on lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily since 2013, hypertension on lisinopril, stage IIA colon cancer resected 02/2023, referred for polyuria and polydipsia since the spring with Na 146, serum osm 300 and urine osm 150. Nocturia 5-6 times. No headaches or visual change.

Exam: BP and pulse normal, euvolemic, mucosa slightly dry.

Desmopressin challenge in clinic: baseline urine osm 150; 2 hours after desmopressin 2 mcg IV, urine osm 162, a rise under 10%.

Impression: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus due to lithium.

Plan:
- Spoke with his psychiatrist. Given ten stable years on lithium and his preference, lithium continues at the current dose with levels every 3 months.
- Start amiloride 5 mg daily, which blunts lithium uptake in the collecting duct.
- Free access to water; avoid thiazides and NSAIDs.
- Amiloride with lisinopril can raise potassium: BMP in 2 weeks, then with each lithium level.
- I am happy to see him again if polyuria persists or kidney function changes.

Nephrology

documents.title: Psychiatry note re lithium
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, phone visit 07/24/2023. Discussed the nephrogenic DI with Mr. Friedman and with nephrology. He has been euthymic on lithium since 2013 and does not want to switch. We agreed to continue lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily with amiloride per nephrology, levels every 3 months, and to revisit if kidney function declines. Next visit in the fall.

documents.title: BMP on amiloride
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Two weeks on amiloride with lisinopril: potassium fine, sodium down from 146. No changes. Patient says he's up maybe 2-3 times a night now.

reports.text: Type 3 home study, one night of valid recording. Respiratory event index (AHI, 4% rule) 24 events per hour, predominantly obstructive hypopneas, worse supine. Oxygen saturation nadir 84%. Snoring recorded for much of the night. Heart rate regular.
reports.conclusion: Moderate obstructive sleep apnea. Auto-titrating CPAP recommended.

documents.title: Sleep study result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discussed the home sleep test: moderate obstructive sleep apnea, AHI 24, low of 84%. He's not surprised. Recommended auto-CPAP 5-15 cm H2O with heated humidifier, mask fitting at the DME supplier, and a sleep medicine visit in 3 months for a compliance check. Order and face-to-face documentation sent to DME. Advised no drowsy driving.

documents.title: Oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Medical oncology, 09/12/2023. Six months after resection of stage IIA ascending colon cancer, on surveillance. Feels well; bowels regular; no bleeding or abdominal pain. Weight stable. Since our last visit he was diagnosed with nephrogenic DI from lithium (on amiloride) and sleep apnea. Exam unremarkable. CEA 2.1. No evidence of recurrence. Next visit with CEA in 6 months; surveillance CT and colonoscopy in February 2024.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Patrick is here for his regular follow-up. Since we last met: oncology chose surveillance for the stage IIA colon cancer (CEA 2.1 this month, fine), nephrology confirmed lithium-related nephrogenic DI and started amiloride, and the sleep study showed moderate OSA. CPAP arrived about three weeks ago; he's getting used to the mask and already sleeping more soundly.

Today no complaints. Urination much better, up once or twice a night. Still drinks a lot of water. No chest pain or shortness of breath; walks most mornings. Doesn't smoke, eats well.

He has been thinking about his father's heart attack at 55 and wants to know if he should take a baby aspirin to prevent one.

Exam: BP 132/84, BMI 27. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
Labs 9/20: LDL 98, HDL 45, TG 150. Lithium 0.9, BMP normal.

A/P
1. Primary prevention, aspirin: no known heart disease. We talked through it: for someone in his situation, daily aspirin offers a small reduction in heart attack risk, offset by a real risk of GI and other bleeding, and current guidance leaves it as an individual call. He would rather not start it. Fine. Continue statin and BP control, which do more.
2. Lithium-induced NDI: better on amiloride. Lithium level 0.9, upper usual range; psychiatry aware.
3. OSA on CPAP: early use going well.
4. HTN, hyperlipidemia: stable, no changes.
5. Flu shot today. COVID updated vaccine when available.

Follow up in 4 months.

medications.sig: Place 1 tablet under the tongue every 5 minutes as needed for chest pain, up to 3; call 911 if not relieved

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 92. Normal axis and intervals. Horizontal ST depression of 1 mm in V2-V4. No ST elevation. No Q waves.
reports.conclusion: Anterior ST depression without ST elevation.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 55% by biplane method. No regional wall motion abnormality. Normal right ventricular size and function. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV systolic function, LVEF 55%, no regional wall motion abnormality.

documents.title: Discharge summary - NSTEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital cardiology service. Admitted 10/04/2023, discharged 10/06/2023.

Presentation: 59M woke at about 4:30 am with heavy central chest pressure into the left arm, sweaty, and came in by ambulance. Aspirin 324 mg given by EMS. ECG with ST depression V2-V4, no elevation. High-sensitivity troponin I 214 ng/L on arrival, peak 1,840 ng/L.

Catheterization 10/04 (right radial): 90% mid-LAD stenosis, treated with one drug-eluting stent with good result. Other vessels with mild irregularities only.
Echo 10/05: LVEF 55%, no wall motion abnormality.

Course uncomplicated; pain free after PCI. Lithium continued, level 0.8. Kidney function stable after contrast.

Diagnoses: NSTEMI; coronary artery disease s/p LAD drug-eluting stent. Also hypertension, hyperlipidemia, bipolar I disorder on lithium, lithium-induced nephrogenic DI, OSA on CPAP, stage IIA colon cancer resected 02/2023.

Discharge medications:
NEW aspirin 81 mg daily, indefinitely
NEW clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months, do not stop without talking to cardiology
NEW metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily
NEW nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed
CONTINUE lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily, amiloride 5 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; cardiology clinic 4-6 weeks; cardiac rehabilitation referral placed. No driving for 1 week, no heavy lifting for a week (radial site).

documents.title: Post-hospital visit - NSTEMI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 6 days after discharge for NSTEMI with a drug-eluting stent to the mid-LAD (10/4). Nine days after we decided against aspirin, he woke up with chest pressure; he says he's glad he called 911 instead of waiting.

Since home: no chest pain, no dyspnea, walking 10-15 minutes twice a day. Radial site bruised but healing. Taking everything, with a pill organizer now. A bit lightheaded standing up fast the first two days, gone now. Mood: shaken but okay; sleeping with CPAP.

Med reconciliation done with patient: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25, NTG SL prn (has not needed), lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, lithium 300 bid, amiloride 5.

Exam: vitals as charted. Right wrist with resolving ecchymosis, radial pulse 2+. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: NSTEMI s/p LAD DES, recovering. Stressed not interrupting clopidogrel. Cardiac rehab: he has the intake call next week. Cardiology visit 11/8. Lithium: level 0.8 in hospital; continue q3 month checks. Discussed the warning signs and when to use nitroglycerin and call 911. RTC January, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, 11/08/2023. Five weeks after NSTEMI with mid-LAD drug-eluting stent. No angina, no dyspnea, no palpitations. Started cardiac rehab this week. Taking aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20; also lithium and amiloride from his other doctors. Vitals reviewed. Exam normal, right radial site healed. ECG sinus rhythm, no acute changes.
Plan: continue DAPT for 12 months from 10/2023, then aspirin alone. Continue current statin. Finish rehab. Return in 4-5 months, sooner for symptoms.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - COVID vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Updated 2023-24 COVID vaccine L deltoid. On clopidogrel and aspirin; pressure held 2 minutes, no bleeding. Says rehab is going well, up to 25 minutes on the bike. No reaction during the wait.

documents.title: Sleep medicine follow-up
documents.author: sleep medicine
documents.body: Sleep medicine clinic, 12/12/2023. Moderate OSA (home study AHI 24, nadir 84%), on auto-CPAP 5-15 with heated humidifier since early September. Download over the last month: used nearly every night for most of the night, residual AHI 3, leak acceptable. Feels more rested, no longer dozing in meetings. Nasal pillows mask fits well. Plan: continue current settings; resupply per schedule; return yearly or with problems.
